mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly increase in GDP (GDPC1) signals expanding economic activity, compressing discount rates on equity cash flows, and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) over a 5-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.0% triggers a monetary tightening cycle, increasing risk aversion and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS remain above 4.0% for 30 days without triggering negative returns, or returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (monetary tightening) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE) creates conflicting signals; their interaction predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as policy uncertainty resolves.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises >0.5% and UNRATE falls >0.2pp in the same month
regime_hint: monetary tightening and labor market improvement
failure_condition: The interaction effect between FEDFUNDS and UNRATE does not predict S&P 500 returns better than individual proxies (p > 0.05 in regression).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime defined by high industrial production (INDPRO > 105) and low inflation (CPIAUCSL < 237), rising supply outpaces demand pressures, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over 3-year periods.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected surge in unemployment (UNRATE > 5.5%) signals labor market stress, reducing consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE stays above 5.5% for 6 months without causing negative returns, or returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high demand (HOUST > 1079) and monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 0.13) creates a favorable environment for equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction of HOUST and FEDFUNDS does not outperform individual proxies in predicting returns (p > 0.05 in regression).

mechanism_narrative: Continued growth in employment (PAYEMS) reflects a strengthening labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate profits, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS employment growth does not correlate with positive 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A post-shock recovery marked by rising demand (RSAFS > 442k) and improving labor conditions (UNRATE < 5.3%) signals economic resilience, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In post-shock recovery, the interaction of RSAFS and UNRATE does not lead to significantly positive returns (p > 0.05).
